fix.notes: The `hide_date` flag follows the same Mustache context-stack pattern used by `hide_source`, `hide_person`, and `hide_top8` — the flag set on the deck_table dict is visible inside `{{#decks}}{{> deckrow}}` because pystache traverses parent contexts. The subtitle p-tag is unstyled; if the site already has a `.subtitle` CSS rule the date will inherit it automatically.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong The "Latest Tournament Top 8" section on the home page showed a Date column, but every deck in the table has the same date (they all come from the same tournament). The column is noise. ## What changed - `decksite/templates/decktable.mustache`: wrapped the `Date` in `{{^hide_date}}...{{/hide_date}}` - `decksite/templates/deckrow.mustache`: wrapped the date `` in `{{^hide_date}}...{{/hide_date}}` - `decksite/templates/home.mustache`: added `{{#subtitle}}

{{subtitle}}

{{/subtitle}}` below the section `

` so the date can be surfaced as a subtitle instead - `decksite/views/home.py`: added `'hide_date': True` and `'subtitle': dtutil.display_date(tournament_decks[0].active_date)` to the tournament deck table dict, hiding the column and showing the shared date below the heading ## Validation - `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (exit 0) - `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 687 passed, 1 skipped, 89 deselected Fixes #12761

triage.fix_sketch: Option A (remove column): wrap the Date <th> in decktable.mustache and the date <td> in deckrow.mustache with {{^hide_date}}...{{/hide_date}}, then add 'hide_date': True to the tournament_decks dict in decksite/views/home.py:setup_decks(). Option B (move date to title): in home.py, fetch the tournament date from the first tournament_deck and append it to the 'Latest Tournament Top 8' title string. Either is ~5–10 lines.
